_meta.purpose: Map Nicomachean Ethics (NE) and Eudemian Ethics (EE) book numbers to Bekker sub-ranges, and handle the 'common books' that belong to BOTH works.
_meta.common_books_note: NE Books V, VI, VII are TEXTUALLY IDENTICAL to EE Books IV, V, VI - the same three books, transmitted once, printed in the NE in the Bekker edition (~1129-1154). They are cited under EITHER work. This creates a genuine double-mapping: a Bekker number in ~1129-1154 belongs to BOTH 'NE V-VII' and 'EE IV-VI'. Scholarship is divided on which work they 'really' belong to (the ordering-of-the-Ethics debate). For the heatmap this matters: a passage in the common books may be cited as 'NE VI 1140a' by one author and 'EE V 1140a' by another - SAME passage, two labels. Decide policy: (a) fold both onto the common-book passage (recommended - it's one text), or (b) keep NE-cited and EE-cited counts separate to STUDY the labelling split (arguably interesting for payoff-2, disciplinary history). Store enough to do either.
_meta.VERIFY: NE start 1094a and EE start 1214a confirmed (Perseus, Hellenica, multiple). _parser_guidance: PRIMARY resolver is still the Bekker number via bekker_ranges.json (which routes 1094-1181 -> NE, 1214-1249 -> EE). This sub-table adds BOOK resolution and the common-books logic.

THE COMMON-BOOKS TRAP: a Bekker number in 1129-1154 lands in the NE's Bekker span, so bekker_ranges alone will always call it 'NE'. But it may have been CITED as 'EE IV/V/VI'. If the adjacent abbreviation says EE/Eth.Eud. AND the number is 1129-1154, record it as a common-book cite (belongs to both), not as a mislabelled NE cite. Do NOT 'correct' an EE-label to NE here - the label is data (who cited it how).

Recommended storage: tag each common-books occurrence with {passage: bekker, ne_book, ee_book, cited_as: 'NE'|'EE'|'ambiguous'}. Then the heatmap can either merge (one text) or split by cited_as (to study the labelling - a payoff-2 disciplinary-history signal: does journal/era X prefer NE or EE labels?).
A bare 'EE IV 1132a' with no Bekker number still resolves: EE IV -> common book -> 1129-1138, cited_as EE.

Watch: EE books VII-VIII jump BACK to 1234+ (after the common books at 1129-1154) - EE's own pagination is non-contiguous because the common books sit in NE's page-space. This is expected, not an error.
